newsitem.title: USA: AMR up on easing interest rates, hope for BA deal.
newsitem.headline: AMR up on easing interest rates, hope for BA deal.

text.p: AMR Corp gained 1-7/8 to 91-3/8 on Monday as interest rates eased slightly and optimism grew about the airline's proposed deal with British Airways Plc .
"Interest rates clipped the wings of airlines for a couple days last week. Things have eased slightly today," said airline analyst Steve Lewins with Gruntal & Co.

On Friday, the yield on the 30-year treasury bond surged over 6.6 percent, before paring its losses to close at 6.51 percent. Long-term interest rate rose about 15 basis points over the course of last week.
On Monday, the yield on the 30-year bond eased slightly to 6.48.
Shares of AMR, the parent of American Airlines, and British Airways also gained on renewed optimism that their proposed marketing alliance will pass regulatory scrutiny, analysts said.
On Friday, British regulators set certain conditions for approving the deal. The demands require the airlines to give up 168 takeoff and landing slots at London Heathrow airport.

Analysts said the demands were reasonable and would not kill the deal. Securing conditional approval by British regulators was a first, positive step in a seemingly endless regulatory process, analysts said.
The Dow Jones transportation index gained 24.66 points to 2298.82, while the broader Dow Jones industrials gained about 82.00 to 6463.94 in closing trade.
